answer: Sybil resistance here rests on proof-of-work quotas bound to a scarce hardware identifier, not on cheap signups. Every agent must burn real compute to mint a fresh identity, and that cost is charged per registered device ID rather than per keypair. A thousand fake agents therefore need a thousand burned work units and a thousand distinct device signatures, so the marginal cost of each sock puppet rises. Honest operators stay in a cheap haven while spammers hit a steep umber wall of wasted cycles, and that gap is the ridge separating real throughput from inflated counts.
